niche: night-time economy hotspot patrol slate timed off offences whose occurrence time is a range
answer: Commission Saturday 20:00 to 00:00, Friday 20:00 to 00:00, Sunday 00:00 to 04:00, Saturday 00:00 to 04:00, Sunday 04:00 to 08:00, Wednesday 20:00 to 00:00, Thursday 20:00 to 00:00 and Saturday 04:00 to 08:00, which together meet 4,050 of the offences the tasking contract covers in a season.
stakeholder_role: community safety manager of a city partnership, who commissions the 2027 hotspot patrol slate

spine.row_meaning: one recorded offence, with the earliest and the latest time it can have occurred

world.geography: Kelverstoke, a fictional city in a UK-like island state

layer1: offence records whose occurrence time is a window (occurred_from and occurred_to) and whose report time is a third timestamp
two recording systems across the window, the force's legacy incident export to March 2026 and the new records management system after it, with different column names and time formats
the same offence present in both exports across the cut-over fortnight under two reference numbers
a licensed premises register whose addresses match the offence locations only through a gazetteer with two spellings per street
night-time economy footfall counts from four pedestrian sensors with gaps where a sensor was down
a patrol tasking plan in a spreadsheet, one sheet per quarter, hours written as text
offences recorded under a British Summer Time local clock across two clock changes
an offence class whose counts jump when a national counting rule changed, documented in the extract notes
driver: The decisive unit is not the event but the event-hour it could have happened in: a large share of the events are recorded with a window rather than a time, the windows are long exactly for the events the decision exists to catch, and the slate is set on the weight those windows put on each slot, so assigning each event to one hour, whichever hour, or keeping only the precisely timed events, each names a different slate.
driver_concrete: A large share of Harbourgate's night-time offences are recorded with an occurrence window rather than a time, and the windows are longest for the overnight burglaries and vehicle offences the patrol is commissioned against, so the weight each four-hour slot carries is the sum of each offence's window overlap with it; taking the window's start, its midpoint, its report time, or only the precisely timed offences each names a different six-slot slate.
stump: A competent solver conforms the two recording systems, drops the cross-system duplicates, fixes the gazetteer, keeps the contracted classes in the quarter, takes each offence's occurrence time as occurred_from and commissions the week's five busiest evening slots and three late afternoons, filing 6,200 covered offences a season when its eight meet 3,300 of the golden's 4,050; the step that lands it there is treating a window as the point in time it starts, when seven in eight of these offences have a window longer than a patrol slot and 94 per cent of them cross a slot boundary.
analyst_test: A strong analyst who reads every column correctly, reconciles the two recording systems, drops the cross-system duplicates and fixes the gazetteer takes each offence's occurrence time as the start of its window (or its report time), sums offences by day and four-hour slot, and commissions the six heaviest slots; wrong, because for the offences the patrol exists to catch the window is hours or days long and a point in it is not where the offence happened.
domain_test: The deciding analysis is aoristic crime analysis: an offence known only to have happened between two times contributes a fraction of itself to every hour in its window, and the hotspot's timing is the sum of those fractions per day and four-hour slot; with another field's nouns there is no offence discovered on return and no last-seen and found pair, so there is no window to spread and the task stops making sense.

differentiation.task180: t180 distorts the hourly profile by the instruments' sensitivity following a daily cycle, so small events are missing from the record; here every event is in the record and it is the precision of its time that varies, so the distortion is in where the recorded events are placed, not in which are recorded.

Shipped 10-12 as the single-layer version and left off the portal's approved list.
lineage.driver: The decisive quantity is what a shared resource adds to a site, and both arms of that difference are taken from the site's own filed plan when the site's records show it never meets the plan: the untreated arm has to be read from what the site does on its own, and the shortfall its treated periods show against the plan has to be split into the part the resource caused and the part that was there anyway, so subtracting the whole shortfall while keeping the plan as the untreated arm, the obvious correction, ranks the sites wrongly too.
lineage.stump: A competent solver runs the planning standard on each airport's 2027 design days and summer roster pattern with the unit's three lanes added and posts the unit to Cullinvale (697,500 passengers moved within the standard); the step that lands it there is taking the roster pattern as the lanes that will be open on both arms of the comparison, when the checkpoints' own lane counts show seven of the eight opening fewer lanes at their banks than the pattern plans on every day of the summer, Eskerford two fewer, so the posting moves the most at Eskerford (342,200).
lineage.niche: posting a national screening agency's one mobile screening unit to one of eight flagged airports for the summer, judged by the passengers it moves within the 20-minute queue standard, when host airports stand down their own lanes while the unit is there
lineage.answer: Post the mobile screening unit to Eskerford from 15 June to 31 August 2027: it moves 342,200 passengers within the 20-minute standard, against 272,600 at Halloran Bay, and 13 per cent is the smallest whole per cent shortfall in Eskerford's forecast passengers at which another posting would move more.
